newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ravers gyrate through Berlin in sunny Love Parade.
newsitem.headline: Ravers gyrate through Berlin in sunny Love Parade.

text.p: Sun blazed down on the world's largest techno music party on Saturday as an international crowd expected to grow to one million people gyrated through the centre of Berlin for the city's ninth annual Love Parade.

Ravers came from around the world to dance behind 38 brightly decorated floats equipped with turbo-powered sound systems down a six-km (four-mile) stretch of an eight-lane boulevard which leads from the landmark Brandenburg Gate.
"We came because it's something you just have to experience," said Cornelius Hummel, a 19-year-old student from Stuttgart dressed in a Scottish kilt and bug-eyed sunglasses.
"Let the sun shine in your heart," he said, quoting the motto of this year's parade.
"I was just curious to see what it was," said a 26-year-old Chinese exchange student. "The mood is really happy."
The annual event, which last year drew 750,000 people, attracts fans of techno, a mix of thundering beats and repetitive electronic riffs supplied by disc jockeys and enormous sound systems.

"We go to clubs in Holland, but this is the real thing -- the mother of them all," said Sjoerd, a business student from Groningen in the Netherlands. "We are not going to sleep tonight if we can help it."

Although Berlin city officials and hundreds of thousands of techno fans love the Love Parade, it has made a few enemies among environmentalists, who object to the heaps of garbage and human waste the event leaves behind.
Environmentalists tried to block the event this year, but city officials, eager to see the big revenues the parade rakes in, agreed to play hosts once again.
An environmental group called One World posted signs in Tiergarten park, which lines both sides of the parade route, saying: "What we do today decides how the world will look tomorrow".
Although right- and left-wing extremists had threatened violence and disruption at the huge street party, police reported no disturbances as the fun got under way.

Berlin regional Interior Minister Joerg Schoenbohm received an anonymous letter thought to have been sent by neo-Nazis in which the author said three anti-tank mines would be laid along the parade route if the event was staged.
Anarchist punks had planned to hold their annual "Chaos Days" riot during the parade as a protest against its commercialism. Some dubbed the would-be rival march a "Hate Parade".
Overcrowded buses, trains and cars with visitors from across Europe bound for the parade caused traffic jams across the country's motorways and up to two-hour delays at Berlin's main train station.

Some people held an impromptu "rave" on Friday evening in front of the Zoologischer Garten station soon after stepping off the platforms, while three thousand others hijacked the posh Kurfuerstendamm shopping avenue for an all-night party.
Most accommodation has been booked for weeks with people coming from as far afield as South Africa, Australia and the United States.
The Love Parade appears to have become an essential stop on any backpacker's European tour.
